headline: High: nullclaw can write broad workspace state while social-auto-upload uploads media, creating default-path data leakage and cascading misuse risks; prompt injection is lower but present via shared files and outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write filesystem, use MCP, and parse browser/web content; social-auto-upload consumes local media/account files and runs in CLI/headless mode. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from one agent influence the other. The pairwise bridge is plausible but not directly documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or file tree
IF one agent ingests the other agent's generated text or files as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of peer-generated files
Add a manual review step before copying outputs
Restrict MCP/file access to read-only where possible

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, conversation history, and workspace files, while social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads media. nullclaw's broad filesystem and network egress make accidental exposure of sensitive workspace contents plausible in default use; the pairwise path is stronger than medium because the data classes are sensitive and the blast radius includes secrets.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or account directory
IF nullclaw is given files containing secrets or conversation history
IF social-auto-upload reads files produced by nullclaw without filtering
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers
Block outbound network for non-upload tasks
Audit file paths before each run

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw can write the filesystem and modify git state, while social-auto-upload is CLI-based and may also mutate local account files. Their concurrency models both support multiple instances, so overlapping writes to shared files or repos can race. I do not see proof of same-dir defaults, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository, workspace, or account file
IF either agent is run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Add file locks around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can generate and act on webhooks, browser actions, and delegated tasks, while social-auto-upload performs publishing workflows. If social-auto-upload treats nullclaw's output as authoritative, a bad instruction or hallucinated fact can cascade into incorrect uploads or account actions. The pathway exists, but I lack direct evidence of default trust, so I choose medium.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload consumes nullclaw-generated captions, metadata, or commands
IF no verification step checks the content before upload or publish
mitigations: Compare generated metadata to source files
Log and diff all handoff payloads

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly handles audit logs, conversation history, and secrets, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to documented gaps and handling discipline. I cite both because the concern is the pair's combined data handling, not a single-agent violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent's workspace
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
